C1.worst_defect: The hero lede says what it is and who it is for, but that it has two parts (a hosted till at app.vendurepos.com plus a server plugin you install) is left to the small grey line under the buttons, "Your own store needs the plugin on your Vendure server first", so in five seconds a buyer cannot tell whether this is a hosted service or a self-installed plugin.
C1.where: home.desktop.01 (line under Live demo / Quick start); home.phone.01

C2.worst_defect: The site never says who builds and maintains VendurePOS, where to report a bug or get help, or on what terms app.vendurepos.com is hosted (free? for how long? any uptime promise?). The footer only offers "MIT licensed. Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS." plus GitHub and npm, so a sceptic cannot judge bus factor or support. Smaller points: the live demo runs ahead of the released plugin ("Refund a sale at the till: Yes" on the demo, "No, not on plugin 0.3.0" on your store; the customer note is demo-only). The ReadOrder gap in the role made by New POS till key has gone unpatched since 2026-10-06 and is worked around on four pages. The phone home shows the till in its phone layout while "tablets and phones ... are not tested yet".
C2.where: home.desktop.02 footer and the 'Live demo or your own store' table; changelog.desktop.01 ('Not in the release notes: in 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 this role has no ReadOrder'); home.phone.01 hero image vs home.phone.04 'Before you start'

C3.worst_defect: Step 4 lists the six permissions the till's administrator needs (TallyPosSell, ReadCatalog, ReadSettings, ReadCustomer, CreateCustomer, ReadOrder) but never says how to make that role and administrator in the Dashboard. It only links to 'Give each cashier their own account', which says just as briefly to 'create a role ... create one administrator per cashier', so the one manual step before the first sale is the least spelled out.
C3.where: quick-start.desktop.02 (4. Enable bearer authentication); connect-a-till text 'Give each cashier their own account'

C4.worst_defect: The changelog covers only the plugin. The till cashiers actually use is 'till app version 0.1.0, built 19 Nov 2026 from vendurepos/app commit cb9bf2c' and has no release notes at all, so nobody can tell what changed in the hosted till or when.

C5.worst_defect: The docs are stock docs-framework chrome (default sidebar, 'Copy Markdown' / 'Open' buttons under every title, identical grey callouts) and the home page is plain black-on-grey with no product colour or mark. It is tidy but generic, which a buyer weighing it against Shopify POS or Square reads as hobby-grade.

C6.worst_defect: Long TypeScript lines wrap mid-expression on 390 px, e.g. generateMigration(config, { name: / 'AddVendurePos', outputDir: / './src/migrations' }) breaks over three lines and .catch(...) over two, which makes the copy-paste code hard to check by eye. The hero till screenshot is cropped after the first two products, so the cart is never shown.

C7.worst_defect: The SoftwareApplication JSON-LD has no softwareVersion and no offers/price. The 'pre-release, plugin 0.3.0' and 'free hosted till' facts appear only in visible text, not in the machine-readable data. The quick-start LCP is 2.6 s (score 0.88), against 2.3 s on /.

overall_worst.defect: Nowhere on the site says who maintains VendurePOS, where to file issues or get support, or the terms of the hosted till at app.vendurepos.com (cost, longevity, no SLA). A sceptic advising a client cannot rule out a one-person side project that may vanish, and the honest limits elsewhere do not make up for that.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 / home.phone.05 footer ('MIT licensed. Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS.' + GitHub, npm, Limitations, Changelog); docs Overview 'Next steps'
overall_worst.fix: Add one short 'Who runs this' paragraph to the Overview and a footer link. It should name the maintainer, link GitHub Issues for bugs and support, and state that app.vendurepos.com is a free static build of the MIT source with no uptime guarantee and that you can self-host it (Connect a till).
